A type of command that affects the social interaction of the character, but doesn't have any direct game effects (such as damage or changing some state). Also known as an Emote. Some socials actually do affect the game, but they are small in number: * /laydown, /sleep, /lie - These socials put you in a prone position that you must stand from to enter combat. * /sit - This social puts you in a sitting position that you must stand from to enter combat. Many emotes are used for Roleplaying

A socket is a special slot on an item into which gems can be inserted to provide bonuses similar to those gained from enchanting. Sockets can be located on every piece of armor; however, each expansion has a different set of armor pieces that can have sockets. Depending on the source, from World of Warcraft: Warlords of Draenor onwards, certain items that don't usually have sockets have a chance to drop with a socket.

A socketed item is an item with one or more sockets which can be filled with special gems. Socketed items were introduced in the Burning Crusade expansion, and function much like jewels from Diablo 2 Lord of Destruction. Sockets do not replace enchantments. So, an item could have up to 3 types of bonuses aside from its default stats : * Temporary improvement ( Sharpening Stone, Wizard Oil, weightstone ) * Permanent Enhancement ( Armor Kit, or enchantment ) * Socketed gems Socketed items can be found in Outland and Northrend, and may be crafted by high level crafters. ]] Snowfall Graveyard is a neutral graveyard found on top of the hill west of Field of Strife and is the only remaining accessible area of Winterax Hold after the avalanche. The actual spawnpoint of the graveyard is located further west, across the rope bridge, in an area known Winterax Hold (although no fortifications or buildings remain). Socket bonus is a jewelcrafting term referring to a bonus when gem and socket matching is achieved. Simply put, a red gem put into a will count towards the socket bonus, but so would an orange or purple gem. A yellow gem for example can still be socketed in a red socket, however, the socket bonus will be disabled, unless the socket is regemmed.

Snow beasts appeared in the canceled Warcraft Adventures. They were white-furred, bestial creatures that dwelt in the Frostwolf Settlement area. Despite not being outwardly hostile to Thrall, the males seemed fond of head butting against competitors, to the point that they could lose their horns, which were described a hollow and sturdy. They were distinctly different from the wendigo that also appeared in the area. Thrall tricked a snow beast into breaking down the door to the cave that contained the Axe of Durotan. When he melted the ice block that contained the axe and cooled the boiling water that the axe sank into, he used the axe to kill the snow beast.

Soggy's Gamble is a town on the southeastern coast of the Dread Wastes founded by the shipwrecked crew of the Mist-Hopper, an Anglers vessel under the command of Captain "Soggy" Su-Dao. The Chittering Coast overlooks the cove to the northeast, the Lonesome Cove is southeast, and Mazu's Overlook is the high bluff to the immediate west. The Anglers here make most of their money by fishing emperor crabs, but they send all kinds of goods from the sea back around the Serpent's Spine, including oils, plants, shark teeth, and rare minerals. San the Sea Calmer runs an inn here named the Chum Bucket.

The Snowspring clan is a furbolg clan found in the Grizzly Hills of Northrend. While less than half of the furbolg population is found in Grizzlemaw, the rest are gathered in clans and scattered throughout the Grizzly Hills. Each clan has its own totem, and when you see one you know you have entered their territory. Because of this it is best to declare yourself openly once you see the totem, since a furbolg may be watching and will not appreciate your trying to sneak past.
